issue_context.title: Improving the logic for auto changing the layout mode
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem?**
The layout mode will change from detail view to tiles randomly in folder. There is not pattern i can see it will randomly change it when I open a folder.

**Describe the solution**
Fix the issue where it's randomly changing the layout mode.

**Additional comment**
Logs in case they can be used to fix how layouts will change automatically.
[debug_fulltrust.txt](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/6290224/debug_fulltrust.txt)
[debug.txt](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/6290223/debug.txt)
comments:
We are working on improving this feature, can you provide details of what kinds of items were in the folders that unexpectedly changed layout modes?
Fyi @d2dyno1
It quite random most of the time mostly exe, dll and folders only directorys.
@yaichenbaum we could add an option to disable Adaptive Layout
@d2dyno1 Before doing that, we should tweak the behavior, I had this issue as well, but I think that once it's fixed, we won't need a setting.
@d2dyno1 Can you adjust the adaptive layout feature to work correctly with the file types Josh mentioned? I can reproduce this issue as well.
@josh-65 Could you share a screen recording of that issue and provide more details on what kind of items were in that folder, their extension, amount.
I can try get a video of it happening. but i have found that there no pattern based on the amount or what's in the folders.

Documents folder turned to grid view with these files in it.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26977075/115959724-86356d80-a505-11eb-80a1-25fcd18aa26c.png)

> Documents folder turned to grid view with these files in it.
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26977075/115959724-86356d80-a505-11eb-80a1-25fcd18aa26c.png)

Ahh.. I see 👀 There's a logic that adaptive layout follows so there's no random guessing. You can take a look at this logic here: https://github.com/files-community/Files/blob/main/Files/Helpers/AdaptiveLayoutHelpers.cs#L11
still would be nice to disable it entirely

Currently I found that the file extensions below will make it go to grid mode when they shouldn't.
ini, bin, sp, dll, docx, pptx, json, wlt, lua, tmp, xml, sys, config, ymal, settings

> still would be nice to disable it entirely

That's fair feedback, before looking into that though, we plan to improve the actual feature. In the meantime, you can turn it off by turning off the option to use individual settings for different locations.
just to let you know I have updated listed the extension that change it to grid mode.
@d2dyno1 Can I assign you this issue?
Sure, I've been bit busy recently but this shouldn't be much work.
This issue should be resolved with #5140.

On 1.5.32 it still an issue for .mrimg (Marcum reflect backup files), .vhdx (Hyper-V hard disk) and sometimes folder only directory.

Updated logs:
[debug_fulltrust.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/6644587/debug_fulltrust.log)
[debug.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/6644589/debug.log)
@josh-65 How many items are in the directory?
usually about 3 to 5. happened with a .vhdx (Hyper-V hard disk) too
This is currently the expected behavior for directories with less than 6 items, but @d2dyno1 is working on changing it.

review_comments: @d2dyno1 How comfortable would you be with making the threshold percentages constant variables? I just prefer to reduce the amount of "magic numbers" if possible.
Sure, can you give some suggestions how to name them? 💡

Some of the weird names we had in Files demonstrate I'm probably the wrong person for that job 😆

@yaichenbaum We need some variable names for these threshold values. 
How about the following:
- `LargeAdaptiveThreshold` for 85.0f
- `MediumAdaptiveThreshold` for 60.0f
- `SmallAdaptiveThreshold` for 25.0f
- `ExtraSmallAdaptiveThreshold` for 15.0f
If these sound weird, then we can drop this suggestion altogether, but it would reduce duplicated use of magic float values.
How about naming them with different confidence levels?
@duke7553 had a good idea in his comment above.
